Giacomo Vianello

Hi, I am Giacomo! I am a Master's student in Control Systems Engineering at the University of Padua, specializing in robotics and intelligent systems.

Currently, I am an intern at the University of Zaragoza within the RoPeRT group (I3A). My research focuses on the integration of Artificial Intelligence and Aerial Vehicles for my Master's thesis, under the guidance of Prof. Ruggero Carli and the supervision of Prof. Eduardo Montijano and David M. Cabello.

Prior to this, I earned my Bachelor's degree in Electronic Engineering from the University of Padua, graduating with a perfect score of 110/110.

I am always open to discussing new ideas, research, or potential collaborations. Feel free to reach out!

Projects

I am passionate about robotics and control systems. Below are some of the projects I have developed, ranging from university assignments to personal challenges in AI and automation.

NMPC for Inverted Pendulum on a Cart using Acados



Course Project - Adaptive and Model Predictive Control, 2026
code | poster | abstract |

Implementation of a Non-linear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) strategy to stabilize an inverted pendulum on a cart. The project leverages the acados solver for high-performance numerical optimization and CasADi for algorithmic differentiation, focusing on real-time feasibility and state/input constraints.

This project explores the use of acados to solve real-time optimal control problems. I modeled the nonlinear dynamics of the inverted pendulum and designed an NMPC controller capable of managing actuator constraints, ensuring system stability even in the presence of disturbances.

Deep Reinforcement Learning for Snake


Giacomo Vianello
Course Project - Reinforcement Learning, 2026
paper | code | abstract |

An implementation of various Deep Reinforcement Learning agents (A2C, PPO, and DDQN) to solve the classic Snake game. The project explores agent performance in both fully and partially observable environments, analyzing how different architectures and reward functions impact the learning stability and final score.

In this project, I developed a custom environment for the Snake game to test different Deep Reinforcement Learning algorithms. I compared policy-gradient methods like PPO and A2C against value-based methods like Double DQN. A significant part of the work involved designing the state representation for partially observable scenarios, where the agent only sees a limited 3x3 or 5x5 grid around its head.

Robotic Manipulation and Cube Swapping with UR5


G Vianello, S Ferracane
Intelligent Robotics - University of Padua, 2026
paper | code | abstract |

A comprehensive ROS2 pipeline for robotic pick-and-place and sorting tasks using a UR5 manipulator. The project integrates MoveIt2 for motion planning, custom C++ servers for kinematics management, and computer vision for real-time color-based object detection and localization.

This project implements an autonomous manipulation pipeline for a UR-5 robotic arm to identify and swap the positions of two AprilTag-equipped cubes. The system integrates real-time pose estimation and color classification with MoveIt-based collision avoidance to reconstruct the table geometry and ensure safe motion planning. By maintaining a consistent virtual scene throughout the execution, the solution achieves a robust pick-and-place sequence within a simulated environment.

Autonomous Navigation and Semantic Goal Seeking


G Vianello, S Ferracane
Intelligent Robotics - University of Padua, 2025
paper | code | abstract |

A ROS2-based autonomous navigation system for a mobile robot in a simulated environment. The project implements a multi-modal architecture combining Nav2 for global path planning, AprilTag detection for semantic goal identification, and a custom Lidar-based controller for stable corridor navigation.

This project implements an autonomous navigation pipeline for a TurtleBot 3 that integrates AprilTag recognition with a hybrid control strategy. The system calculates target goals between detected markers and transitions from global Nav2 planning to a custom LiDAR-based PD controller for stable corridor traversal. By combining modular C++ orchestration with real-time DBSCAN clustering, the robot effectively localizes cylindrical obstacles while maintaining seamless mission continuity.

ROS2 Integration of Vision-Language Models


Giacomo Vianello
Research Internship - University of Zaragoza, 2025
code | abstract |

Development of a ROS2 framework to integrate Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for aerial robotics. The project enables real-time scene understanding and captioning using both local models (like BLIP and SmolVLM) and cloud-based APIs (Gemini), providing a modular pipeline for high-level robot perception.

Prior to my internship at the University of Zaragoza, I developed this ROS2-based infrastructure to bridge the gap between high-level semantic reasoning and robotic platforms. The system is organized into two main packages: vlm_api_package, which interfaces with the Gemini API for powerful cloud-based reasoning, and vlm_local_package, which implements local inference using SmolVLM and BLIP for privacy and edge computing scenarios.

Bayesian Parameter Estimation for 2R Manipulators


F Baldini, F Berti, S Ferracane, S Michielon, G Vianello
Estimation and Filtering - University of Padua, 2025
paper | code | abstract |

Application of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods to estimate the dynamic parameters of a 2-DOF planar manipulator. The project uses a Bayesian approach to infer link masses and lengths from noisy joint torque and trajectory data, comparing different sampling strategies and prior distributions.

This project implements a Bayesian framework using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) to estimate the friction parameters of a 2-degree-of-freedom (2R) planar robotic manipulator. By employing the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm, the system identifies both linear and nonlinear friction components from noisy torque and velocity data.
